definitions.gloss: reap what you sow, you get what you deserve
definitions.explanation: Suffering the consequences of one's own actions. Originally a Buddhist concept of karma.

examples.japanese: ⟦それ→それ：00994_sore⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{自業自得|じごうじとく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦しか→しか：09959_shika⟧⟦{言|い}えない→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: I can only say you brought it on yourself.

examples.japanese: ⟦{嘘|うそ}をついた→嘘をつく：21763_usowotsuku⟧⟦{結果|けっか}→結果：02486_kekka⟧、⟦{信用|しんよう}→信用：03267_shinyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{失|うしな}った→失う：01887_ushinau⟧。{自業自得|じごうじとく}⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。
examples.english: As a result of lying, you lost trust. You got what you deserved.

examples.japanese: ⟦{勉強|べんきょう}しなかった→勉強：00770_benkyou⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{不合格|ふごうかく}→不合格：05139_fugoukaku⟧⟦になった→なる：01970_naru⟧。{自業自得|じごうじとく}⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: I didn't study, so I failed. I reaped what I sowed.

notes:
{自業自得|じごうじとく} is a Buddhist-origin ⟦{四字熟語|よじじゅくご}→四字熟語：15663_yojijukugo⟧ meaning "you reap what you sow." It expresses that one's fate is determined by one's own actions (karma).

FORMS:
{自|じ} (self) + ⟦{業|ごう}→業：28169_gou⟧ (deeds/karma) + {自|じ} (self) + ⟦{得|とく}→得：12563_toku⟧ (obtain) = one obtains the results of one's own deeds

USAGE:
- Often used when someone suffers consequences of their own bad choices
- Can sound harsh or judgmental when directed at others
- Used as a noun or as a predicate with ⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {自業自得|じごうじとく}⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧: You brought it on yourself
- {自業自得|じごうじとく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦しか→しか：09959_shika⟧⟦{言|い}えない→言う：00515_iu⟧: I can only say it's self-inflicted
- ⟦それ→それ：00994_sore⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{自業自得|じごうじとく}⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧: That's your own doing

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{因果応報|いんがおうほう}→因果応報：05948_ingaouhou⟧: karmic retribution (more neutral)
- ⟦{身|み}→身：01764_mi⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{出|で}た→出る：00513_deru⟧⟦{錆|さび}→錆：03887_sabi⟧: rust from one's own body (similar meaning)
- ⟦{蒔|ま}いた→蒔く：02419_maku⟧⟦{種|たね}→種：02157_tane⟧: reap what you sow (lit. seeds you planted)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Originates from Buddhist teachings on karma. Use carefully, as it can come across as unsympathetic or blaming.
